_doc: S1.5 — the channel the kit routed you to (ERA1_LOGIC_v1 §3, register: felt). The warmth is real; the routing is the harm. The DM arrives BY NAME — the network knew you were coming (v0.7 §6). Period terms ('struggle', 'SSA') appear in ambient speech, not as lectures. ⚑ draft for Sérgio. ⚑ S142 (2026-09-13) — THE CHANNEL TALKS TO HIM. Until now the room never addressed Daniel: eleven lines of ambient, then Rob's DM. Now the room notices him after its fourth line (`welcome`, by name), he answers with the one line he is given (`channelReply` — press-only, the narrowed voice), two people answer him back (`afterReply`), and it is LUME — the kindest voice in the room — who points him at Rob. The warmth is real and it is the routing. Rob's DM then opens by name and quotes the channel: he was watching. Nothing here speaks for anyone; every line is invented.

dcc._doc: ⚑ S186 — yes.gif, SENT (Sérgio, 2026-09-28: 'the poster using the YES online, as something sent to Daniel'; 'you have to accept, it's not optional (pressure)'). Once Rob's private message has landed, he sends an image over DCC — how pictures travelled in mIRC in 1997. Accept is the only live answer; Ignore is drawn dead (R3-26's convention: shown to be dead, not hidden). The image opens in a viewer that owns the screen until closed (os.ts); then Rob says one more line, and only then does the channel hand on (the hook). src/desktop/apps/yesPoster.ts draws it.
